brief.situation_en: Maria tells Raimo the bedroom is cold.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Moi! Mun makkarin patteri on kylmä.
lines.text_kirja: Hei! Minun makuuhuoneeni patteri on kylmä.
lines.gloss_en: Hi! The radiator in my bedroom is cold.

judge.reason: Makkari is colloquial for makuuhuone (bedroom); mun/minun, moi/hei are register differences. Same meaning.

puhe.text: Moi! Mun makkarin patteri on kylmä.

kirja.text: Hei! Minun makuuhuoneeni patteri on kylmä.

judge.reason: Olkkari is colloquial for olohuone (living room); the spoken form is just a short nominative form, same meaning.
Siel is a dropped-ending form of siellä; same meaning.

lines.speaker: Raimo
lines.text_puhe: Sit patteris on ilmaa. Mä tuun ja ilmaan sen.
lines.text_kirja: Sitten patterissa on ilmaa. Minä tulen ja ilmaan sen.
lines.gloss_en: Then there's air in the radiator. I'll come and bleed it.

judge.reason: Sit/sitten, patteris/patterissa, mä tuun/minä tulen are register variants; same content.

puhe.text: Sit patteris on ilmaa. Mä tuun ja ilmaan sen.

kirja.text: Sitten patterissa on ilmaa. Minä tulen ja ilmaan sen.

judge.reason: Kauanks is colloquial kauanko; same question.
Vaan/vain, viis/viisi, minuuttii/minuuttia; same meaning, five minutes.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Good! It's really cold in the room.

judge.reason: Huonees/huoneessa and tosi/todella are register differences; same meaning.

lines.speaker: Raimo
lines.text_puhe: Kohta on lämmin. Mä tuun heti.
lines.text_kirja: Pian on lämmin. Minä tulen heti.
lines.gloss_en: It'll be warm soon. I'm coming right away.

judge.reason: Kohta and pian both mean soon; mä tuun/minä tulen heti is the same. Same meaning.

puhe.text: Kohta on lämmin. Mä tuun heti.

kirja.text: Pian on lämmin. Minä tulen heti.

forms.why_en: Moi is the everyday spoken hello. Books and formal texts write hei.
Minä with -n: minun pitää means I have to. Speech shortens it to mun.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for my
forms.why_en: Adds -ni for 'my': makuuhuone becomes makuuhuoneeni. Speech uses the short word makkari: mun makkarin.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
The form of olla, to be, for he, she or it. People say it the same way.

Adds -ssa for 'in': olohuone becomes olohuoneessa. Speech uses the short word olkkari: olkkaris.
Siellä means there. Speech shortens -llä to -l: Siellä becomes Siel.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.

Speech shortens sitten to sit. Books write sitten.
Adds -ssa for 'in': patteri becomes patterissa. Speech shortens -ssa to -s: patterissa becomes patteris.
Adds -a for an amount of something: ilma becomes ilmaa, 'some air'.
Speech shortens minä to mä. Books write minä.
Adds -en for 'I': tulla becomes tulen. Speech says tuun.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.

forms.lemma_meaning_en: to let air out, to bleed (a radiator)
forms.why_en: Ilmata, to let air out. With minä the verb ends in -n: ilmaan.
Se with -n when the whole thing is the object: kirjoittaa sen.
Kauan, long, with -ko to ask. Speech says -ks: kauanks.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Speech says vaan. Books write vain.
Speech drops the final i: viisi becomes viis.
After a number the noun takes the partitive: kymmenen minuuttia. Speech turns -ia into -ii.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Adds -ssa for 'in', with an extra e: huone becomes huoneessa. Speech shortens -ssa to -s: huoneessa becomes huonees.
Books write todella. In speech people use tosi, 'really', instead.
Speech often says kohta 'in a moment' instead of pian.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
